subject: VM evidence briefing & remediation tempo attestation (FinTrust)
summary: Delivering vulnerability management evidence packet (scan cadence, retention, CVE remediation SLAs) and a signed attestation for FinTrust SIG/SOC2 review.
messages:
From: Erin O'Leary <erin.oleary@fintrust.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com
Cc: security-requests@fintrust.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: VM evidence + attestation for SIG deep-dive

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As part of our SIG review and upcoming SOC 2 refresh, can you provide the following for our security team?

- A short evidence packet describing your vulnerability management cadence (authenticated scans cadence, credentialed vs unauthenticated),
- Current CVE remediation SLAs by severity and confirmation those SLAs applied to the last 90 days,
- A signed attestation we can include in the SIG record that Redwood enforces the stated cadence and SLAs, and
- Any supporting artifacts (scan index, remediation logs, owner roster).

Target deadline: COB Monday 2027-04-04 if possible — we have a compliance checkpoint on Tuesday. If you need an alternative timeline let me know.

Thanks — really appreciate it.
Erin O'Leary
Security Manager, FinTrust
Erin.OLeary@fintrust.com
[FinTrust | Compliance Team]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com>
To: Erin O'Leary <erin.oleary@fintrust.com>
Cc: security-requests@fintrust.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 12:45:13 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence + attestation for SIG deep-dive

Erin —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver that packet and a signed attestation by your deadline. High-level answers up front, details and artifacts attached below.

Quick overview:
- Scan cadence: authenticated weekly (credentialed scanner against active services), unauthenticated external scan weekly, full authenticated nightly for critical infra (edge + control plane). Monthly full‑surface authenticated scan for customer-facing workloads.
- Remediation SLAs (applied to tracked CVEs in last 90 days): Critical/P1: 7 calendar days; High/P2: 30 calendar days; Medium/P3: 90 calendar days; Low/P4: evaluated case-by-case. For cloud-managed dependencies we follow vendor advisories and apply compensating controls when appropriate.
- Evidence retention: scan results and triage logs retained 12 months; remediation logs and owner timestamps retained 24 months.

Attached:
- vm-scan-index-202703.pdf (index of scans and scope)
- cve-remediation-log-202703.csv (exported remediation ledger for last 90 days)

We'll follow up with a short signed attestation doc and a formal DocuSign link. If you need us to map specific CVE IDs from our log to your tracker, say the word and we will cross-reference.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com
[Attachment: vm-scan-index-202703.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: cve-remediation-log-202703.csv (CSV)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence + attestation for SIG deep-dive

Hannah / Monica —

A couple of clarifications for the attestation wording and artifacts Erin asked for:

1) Scan types & cadence to call out explicitly in the attestation:
   - Weekly credentialed internal network scan (Nessus/Trivy hybrid)
   - Weekly unauthenticated external perimeter scan (Qualys)
   - Nightly rapid vulnerability sweep for critical infra (edge/control plane)
   - Monthly full authenticated application stack scan (staging mirrors prod)
2) SLA measurement: we calculate SLA windows from the timestamp when a CVE is triaged and assigned an owner (owner + assignment timestamp recorded in remediation ledger). Include sample rows in the CSV export.
3) Exceptions: documented exceptions and compensating controls are appended and signed by engineering leads — keep that list in the evidence packet.

I'll add a short template paragraph for the signed attestation we can paste into the DocuSign envelope. Also recommending we include a one-page appendix with retention policy snippet (12/24 months).

-Jonas

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com>
To: Erin O'Leary <erin.oleary@fintrust.com>
Cc: security-requests@fintrust.com, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 17:40:06 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence + attestation for SIG deep-dive

Erin —

Per our thread above, please find the attached VM evidence packet and our signed attestation. Summary highlights:

- We run a blended cadence: weekly external unauthenticated scans, weekly internal credentialed scans, nightly critical infra sweeps, and monthly full authenticated application scans.
- SLAs are enforced from triage assignment: Critical (P1) = 7 days, High (P2) = 30 days, Medium (P3) = 90 days. We track assignment timestamps and remediation closure in the remediation ledger.
- Logs and scan exports retained as noted: scan outputs (12 months), remediation logs (24 months).
- Exceptions/compensating controls are documented and signed by engineering owners; examples included in the appendix.

Attached artifacts (for SIG/CAIQ):
- vm-scan-index-202703.pdf — scope and cadence matrix (PDF)
- cve-remediation-log-202703.csv — last 90 days remediation ledger (CSV)
- vm-attestation-letter-signed.pdf — signed attestation (PDF)

DocuSign envelope (signed copy) and HubSpot record have been uploaded here for your convenience: https://drive.redwood.example.com/fintrust/vm-evidence-2027-03 (DocuSign copy included). HubSpot:FT-2027-0934.

If you want a CSV filtered to a specific set of CVE IDs or a side-by-side with your tracker, we can produce that within 24 hours. Let me know if the attestation wording needs any tweaks for your SIG record.

Thanks — happy to walk through the packet on a short call if that helps.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com
[Attachment: vm-attestation-letter-signed.pdf (PDF)]
